name: Marcus Chilton
notes: Defeated Raven by pinfall (finisher "Da Bomb") on Wednesday Night Warriors II, 7 March 1997.
caption: Won his AWA debut match with a stunner he calls "Da Bomb."

name: Raven

identity.note: A common ring name already carried by several other registry entries; no primary-source evidence connects this AWA persona to any of them, or to the real wrestler Raven (Scott Levy) -- no portrayal claim is made in the held record.

notes: Lost to Marcus Chilton by pinfall on Wednesday Night Warriors II, 7 March 1997, after a high-flying sequence including a top-rope flying cross body.
caption: A high-flying AWA original whose top-rope offense nearly ended his debut opponent early.

name: Jarred Tokarek
notes: Billed from Nanaimo BC as "AC's invasion of the AWA" -- an in-fiction crossover reference to the do-not-merge guard entity "the AC's AWA." Lost to Nik Nyce by count-out on Wednesday Night Warriors II, 7 March 1997.
caption: A 347-pound power wrestler billed as an invader from a rival, same-acronym AWA.

name: Curtis Hansen

tenures.note: The character's own EMWC-broadcast backstory narrates continuous history from training in Boris Malenko's gym, through "CHAOS!!!" and "the AWA," to the EMWC by name; the same opponent (The Inkinator) recurs in both tenures — primary-source grounds for reading this as one continuous character across american-wrestling-association-1997 and emwc.

notes: Won the main-event triangle match on Wednesday Night Warriors II (7 March 1997) over The Inkinator and "The Baddass" Remy Boudreaux, pinning The Inkinator after Boudreaux eliminated himself over the top rope. Also attested, at primary-source grade (the character's own narrated continuity), in the EMWC's own served corpus: teamed with estranged former partner Kevin Slater to defeat Tonnage and Biff McGriff on An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998), earning a EMWC North American Championship shot, then turned on Slater with a chair after the win.
caption: Carried a continuous career from the AWA into the EMWC, where he turned on his own tag partner after a big win.

name: Remy Boudreaux
notes: Billed as a former AWA North American Champion. Eliminated himself over the top rope in the main-event triangle match on Wednesday Night Warriors II (7 March 1997). A recap montage on the same broadcast depicts him losing the North American title to Kevin Slater in an undated prior match.
caption: A former AWA North American Champion who eliminated himself from a triangle match rather than let a rival win it.

name: The Inkinator

tenures.note: Same distinctive ring name as this entity's own AWA tenure, and the same opponent (Curtis Hansen) recurs; presumed the same continuous character rather than an independent coincidence, at presumed grade pending stronger corroboration (no operator or roster document ties the two tenures directly).

notes: Pinned by Curtis Hansen in the main-event triangle match on Wednesday Night Warriors II, 7 March 1997. Also attested, at presumed grade, in the EMWC's own served corpus: won a twenty-man battle royal for a same-night EMWC World Heavyweight Championship shot against Gabriel Whitecross on An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998), aligned there with The Druid and Mass Pandemonium as "The Prophecy."
caption: Pinned in an AWA main-event triangle match, and years later won an EMWC battle royal for a title shot.

name: Nik Nyce
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #50, tagged SJPW, TCW, AWA. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Billed "The Perfectionist" and a reigning BAHW Television Champion, he ran concurrent 1997 tenures in the AWA (a March count-out win) and SJPW (a May main event and a December title-eliminator build) before ranking #50 in the RSPWF Top 200.

tenures.note: His own handler posted this federation's own recruitment notice in June 1997, and the operator thanks him by name for "a helluva 8 months with Nik Nyce terrorizing the AWA" (14 Nov 1997) -- the primary-source resolution naming which AWA his 1997 RSPWF Top 200 tag (#50) belongs to.

tenures.source: promotions/sjpw/archive/ring-wars-3may1997.html (already served -- main event, 3 May 1997, vs. the returning "former 3 time world champion" Akira Hashimoto, billed "The Perfectionist" Nik Nyce); promotions/sjpw/archive/control-center-7may1997.html (already served -- a follow-up feud-angle segment, 7 May 1997, naming him repeatedly); promotions/sjpw/archive/year-end-review-dec1997.html (already served -- the operator's own year-end recap, 16 Dec 1997, calling him "one of the most reliable handlers in SJPW," naming active feuds with Dan Kauffman, Lance Smith and Alex Akira, and a challenge to Shinji Hamada for the now-vacant All Asian Heavyweight Championship).
tenures.note: This wing's own already-served May-December 1997 pages independently place the SAME wrestler as an active SJPW roster member, running concurrently with (not instead of) the already-attested AWA tenure above -- both promotions' own documents name him by the same ring name with no contradiction.
